ubuntu.name: Ubuntu
ubuntu.description: The most popular desktop Linux distribution. Massive community, commercial support from Canonical, and the widest software compatibility of any distro. Ubuntu 25.10 is current; 26.04 LTS 'Resolute Raccoon' lands April 23, 2026 with GNOME 50, Wayland-only sessions, kernel 7.0, and Rust-based core utilities.
cons: Snap packages can be slow to launch
Canonical's commercial priorities sometimes conflict with community

mint.name: Linux Mint
mint.description: The most Windows-like Linux experience. Ships Cinnamon desktop with no Snaps, excellent out-of-the-box usability, and rock-solid Ubuntu LTS base. Mint 22.3 'Zena' (January 2026) is current; Mint 23 — based on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS — is targeted for Christmas 2026 under a new longer release cadence.
pros: Most familiar experience for Windows users

lmde.name: LMDE
lmde.description: Linux Mint Debian Edition — the same Mint experience built directly on Debian Stable instead of Ubuntu. Insurance policy for the Mint project and a great choice for Debian fans who want Cinnamon.
pros: Pure Debian base without Ubuntu layer
Same Mint tools and Cinnamon experience
Longer support cycle than Ubuntu-based Mint

fedora.name: Fedora
fedora.description: Red Hat's community distribution. Fedora 43 (October 2025) ships RPM 6.0, DNF 5, GNOME 49 Wayland-only, kernel 6.17, and Python 3.14. Fedora 44 with GNOME 50 and KDE Plasma 6.6 is now expected April 28, 2026 after blocker-bug delays. The proving ground for RHEL technologies with strong privacy defaults.
pros: Latest stable software without rolling risk
cons: Short support cycle (13 months per release)
No proprietary codecs out of the box

fedora_silverblue.name: Fedora Silverblue
fedora_silverblue.description: Fedora's immutable desktop variant using OSTree. The base system is read-only with atomic updates and rollbacks. Apps are installed via Flatpak or toolbox containers.
cons: Steeper learning curve for package management

arch.name: Arch Linux
arch.tagline: Keep it simple, build it yourself
arch.description: A rolling-release distribution with a minimal base. You build your system from scratch using pacman and the AUR. The Arch Wiki is the best documentation in all of Linux.

debian.name: Debian
debian.description: The grandfather of Ubuntu, Mint, and hundreds of derivatives. Famous for rock-solid stability and 69,000+ packages. Debian 13 'Trixie' (released August 2025; current point release 13.4 from March 14, 2026) is the active stable.

opensuse.name: openSUSE
opensuse.description: Two flavors: Tumbleweed (rolling) and Leap (stable). YaST is the most powerful graphical system configuration tool in Linux. Strong enterprise heritage from SUSE.
pros: Btrfs snapshots with Snapper by default

opensuse_aeon.name: openSUSE Aeon
opensuse_aeon.description: openSUSE's immutable desktop with GNOME and Btrfs transactional updates. The base system auto-updates atomically; apps are installed via Flatpak. Aeon (GNOME) and Kalpa (KDE) variants.

popos.name: Pop!_OS
popos.description: System76's distribution featuring COSMIC — a Rust-based desktop environment built from scratch. COSMIC Epoch 1 shipped December 2025 in Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS; rolling point releases (1.0.10 in April 2026) bring Wayland-native tiling, polished productivity workflows, and excellent NVIDIA support.
cons: COSMIC is young — some rough edges remain

manjaro.name: Manjaro
manjaro.description: An Arch-based distribution with a user-friendly installer, hardware detection, and a delayed package buffer for extra stability. Bridges the gap between beginner-friendly and rolling-release power.
pros: Arch packages without the manual setup
cons: Delayed packages can break AUR compatibility
Not pure Arch — some community friction

zorin.name: Zorin OS
zorin.description: Designed specifically for Windows and macOS migrants. Beautiful interface with switchable layouts that mimic Windows 11, macOS, or ChromeOS. Zorin OS 18.1 (April 2026) is based on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, adds a new Lite edition for older PCs, ships LibreOffice 26.2, and detects 240+ Windows app installers.
cons: Limited customization in free Core edition

endeavouros.name: EndeavourOS
endeavouros.description: A graphical Arch installer that stays close to vanilla Arch. The 2026.03.06 'Titan' release ships KDE Plasma 6.6, Linux 6.19.6, Calamares 26.03, and Firefox 148. The community is famously friendly and welcoming.
cons: Can still break like any Arch system

cachyos.name: CachyOS
cachyos.description: The hottest Arch derivative in 2025–2026, topping DistroWatch. Features BORE scheduler, CPU-targeted builds (x86-64-v3/v4), AutoFDO-profiled kernels, and a Calamares installer with animated desktop previews. April 2026 ships Linux 6.19, KDE Plasma 6.6, and Proton-CachyOS for gaming.
pros: BORE scheduler + AutoFDO-profiled kernel for top performance
cons: Custom pacman fork may cause compatibility quirks
Performance focus may not matter on older hardware

nixos.name: NixOS
nixos.description: Your entire system defined in a single configuration file. Atomic upgrades, instant rollbacks, and fully reproducible environments. The largest package repository (100,000+ packages in Nixpkgs).

tails.name: Tails
tails.description: A portable OS that routes all traffic through Tor and leaves no trace. Boots from USB, forgets everything on shutdown. Used by journalists, activists, and privacy advocates worldwide.
pros: Amnesic — leaves no trace on disk
Portable — boots from USB on any computer
cons: Cannot persist data without extra setup

qubes.name: Qubes OS
qubes.description: Uses Xen hypervisor to run every application in an isolated virtual machine. Endorsed by Edward Snowden and the Freedom of the Press Foundation. The most security-focused desktop OS available.
pros: Isolates work, personal, and untrusted activities

whonix.name: Whonix
whonix.description: A two-VM approach to privacy: a Gateway VM routes all traffic through Tor, while a Workstation VM runs your apps. IP leaks are architecturally impossible. Runs inside VirtualBox, KVM, or Qubes.
pros: Works inside any host OS via VM
Can run inside Qubes for extra hardening

elementary.name: elementary OS
elementary.description: macOS-inspired aesthetics with the Pantheon desktop. Focuses on design, simplicity, and a curated AppCenter with pay-what-you-want apps. elementary OS 8 is based on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.
cons: Not for power users or tinkerers

void.name: Void Linux
void.description: Fully independent distribution with its own package manager (xbps), init system (runit), and optional musl libc builds. No systemd. Fast, lean, and principled.
pros: musl libc option for minimal footprint
cons: Fewer packages than Arch or Debian
Limited documentation compared to Arch Wiki

mxlinux.name: MX Linux
mxlinux.description: A cooperative venture between antiX and MX communities. Excellent on older hardware with great built-in MX Tools suite. Based on Debian Stable for rock-solid reliability.

antix.name: antiX
antix.description: Ultra-lightweight Debian Stable derivative for very old hardware. Can run on 256MB RAM. Uses IceWM and Fluxbox window managers. No systemd.
pros: Runs on extremely old hardware (256MB RAM)

alpine.name: Alpine Linux
alpine.description: Security-oriented, lightweight distro built on musl libc and BusyBox. The de facto standard for Docker container base images. ~5MB base image. OpenRC init system.
cons: musl libc breaks some glibc-dependent software

gentoo.name: Gentoo
gentoo.description: Source-based distribution where you compile every package with your chosen USE flags and optimizations. Maximum control over every binary running on your system.

rocky.name: Rocky Linux
rocky.description: A 1:1 RHEL-compatible rebuild created after CentOS shifted to Stream. Built for production servers with 10-year support lifecycle. Co-founded by CentOS co-creator Gregory Kurtzer.
cons: Not suitable for desktop daily use

alma.name: AlmaLinux
alma.description: Another RHEL-compatible rebuild, backed by CloudLinux Inc. ABI-compatible with RHEL for seamless enterprise migration. Strong cloud provider support.
pros: Wide cloud provider support (AWS, Azure, GCP)

rhel.name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux
rhel.description: The commercial enterprise Linux standard. 10-year support, certified hardware/software ecosystem, and professional support from Red Hat (IBM). Free for up to 16 systems via developer subscription.

bazzite.name: Bazzite
bazzite.description: An immutable Fedora Atomic-based gaming OS. Drop-in SteamOS replacement for desktops, HTPCs, and handhelds. Boots to Steam Big Picture or KDE/GNOME desktop. Part of the Universal Blue project.
cons: Immutable model unfamiliar to traditional Linux users
Harder to customize than standard distros

nobara.name: Nobara
nobara.description: A Fedora fork by GloriousEggroll (the Proton-GE maintainer). Pre-configured with gaming tools, codecs, custom kernel optimizations, and falcond for per-game CPU tuning. KDE Plasma default.
pros: Codecs and drivers included out of box
cons: One-person passion project — bus factor risk

garuda.name: Garuda Linux
garuda.description: An Arch-based distro with flashy aesthetics (Dragonized), gaming optimizations, Btrfs + Snapper snapshots, and pre-installed gaming tools. Mokka edition offers a calmer Catppuccin theme.
pros: Gaming Edition comes ready to play

steamos.name: SteamOS
steamos.tagline: Valve's gaming OS for Steam Deck
steamos.description: Valve's Arch-based OS powering the Steam Deck. Boots to Game Mode (Big Picture) or a KDE Plasma desktop. Immutable base with Flatpak for desktop apps. SteamOS 3.7.20 (March 2026) adds the NTSync driver, official Legion Go S support, and limited support for other AMD-powered handhelds.
pros: Built specifically for gaming by Valve
cons: Not officially supported on non-Deck hardware

solus.name: Solus
solus.description: An independent, curated rolling-release distro with its own Budgie desktop environment. Focuses on a polished desktop experience with careful package curation. Revived under new leadership in 2023.
pros: Curated rolling release — tested before shipping
cons: eopkg is unique — no cross-distro skills

kali.name: Kali Linux
kali.description: The industry-standard penetration testing distribution. Ships 600+ security tools pre-installed. Based on Debian Testing. Not designed as a daily-driver desktop OS.
cons: Not designed for daily desktop use
Running as root by default was a past issue
Misused by people who don't understand it

parrot.name: Parrot OS
parrot.description: Security-focused Debian derivative with Home (privacy/daily use) and Security (pentesting) editions. Lighter than Kali and more suitable as a daily driver for security professionals.
pros: Home Edition works as a privacy daily driver
Lighter than Kali with similar security tools
cons: Pentesting tools overkill for most users

kubuntu.name: Kubuntu
kubuntu.description: Official Ubuntu flavor featuring KDE Plasma desktop. Same Ubuntu base with LTS support but a more customizable, Windows-like interface. KDE Plasma 6.6 on the upcoming 26.04 LTS (April 23, 2026) — Kubuntu retains LTS status this cycle.
cons: KDE can feel complex for beginners
Can be heavier than GNOME on some hardware

xubuntu.name: Xubuntu
xubuntu.description: Official Ubuntu flavor with Xfce desktop. Lighter than GNOME while maintaining full Ubuntu compatibility. Good for mid-range and older hardware.
cons: Xfce looks dated to some users
Fewer modern DE features than KDE/GNOME

lubuntu.name: Lubuntu
lubuntu.description: Official Ubuntu flavor targeting older computers and resource-constrained hardware. Uses LXQt desktop environment for minimal resource usage while keeping Ubuntu compatibility.

ubuntu_mate.name: Ubuntu MATE
ubuntu_mate.description: Official Ubuntu flavor with the MATE desktop — a continuation of GNOME 2. Traditional desktop layout that's intuitive and resource-efficient. Great Raspberry Pi support. Note: Ubuntu MATE will not carry LTS status on 26.04 due to limited contributor resources.

kde_neon.name: KDE neon
kde_neon.description: The latest KDE Plasma desktop on a stable Ubuntu LTS base. Maintained by the KDE project itself. You always get the newest KDE on release day, with Ubuntu's rock-solid foundation.
pros: Absolute latest KDE on release day
cons: Not a full distro — focused on KDE showcase
Base Ubuntu packages can be old

deepin.name: deepin
deepin.description: Chinese-developed distribution with the stunning Deepin Desktop Environment (DDE). Known for some of the most beautiful default aesthetics in Linux. Based on Debian Stable.
pros: Arguably the most beautiful Linux desktop
cons: Chinese origin raises privacy concerns for some

artix.name: Artix Linux
artix.description: An Arch Linux fork that replaces systemd with your choice of runit, OpenRC, s6, or dinit. For users who want Arch's rolling packages and AUR without systemd.
pros: Arch packages and AUR without systemd
Choice of init: runit, OpenRC, s6, dinit
cons: Some Arch packages need systemd patches

slackware.name: Slackware
slackware.description: The oldest actively maintained Linux distribution (since 1993). BSD-style init, no automatic dependency resolution, and a philosophy of simplicity and Unix tradition.
pros: No dependency auto-resolution — you learn everything

pclinuxos.name: PCLinuxOS
pclinuxos.description: A rolling-release, RPM-based distro with KDE Plasma as the primary desktop. Focuses on providing a simple, out-of-the-box experience. Loyal, long-standing community.

peppermint.name: Peppermint OS
peppermint.description: A lightweight Debian-based distro using Xfce. Designed for cloud-centric workflows and web applications. Very low resource footprint with a clean, minimal interface.

bodhi.name: Bodhi Linux
bodhi.description: A minimal Ubuntu LTS-based distro featuring the Moksha desktop (fork of Enlightenment). Extremely lightweight while offering a unique, customizable desktop experience.

puppy.name: Puppy Linux
puppy.description: An ultra-lightweight family of distros that load entirely into RAM. Boots from USB/CD in seconds on ancient hardware. Saves session to a persistent file. Incredibly fast once loaded.
pros: Entire OS runs in RAM — blazing fast
cons: Not suitable for modern desktop workflows

sparky.name: SparkyLinux
sparky.description: A Debian-based distro available in Stable and Rolling (Debian Testing) editions. Offers multiple desktop environments and a "MinimalGUI" for advanced users to build from scratch.
cons: Rolling edition can have Debian Testing issues

bunsenlabs.name: BunsenLabs
bunsenlabs.description: Successor to CrunchBang. A minimalist Debian-based distro with preconfigured Openbox window manager, tint2 panel, and conky. For users who love a clean, keyboard-driven workflow.
cons: Very DIY for anything beyond basics

mageia.name: Mageia
mageia.description: A community fork of the historic Mandriva Linux. Features the Mageia Control Center (MCC) for system administration and a friendly, community-driven development process.
pros: Mageia Control Center for easy admin

tinycore.name: Tiny Core Linux
tinycore.description: A minimal Linux distribution at just 11MB (Core) or 23MB (TinyCore with GUI). Loads entirely into RAM, with extensions loaded on demand. An educational tool and embedded systems platform.

openmandriva.name: OpenMandriva
openmandriva.description: The direct continuation of Mandriva Linux. Notable for being one of the few distros built entirely with Clang/LLVM. Offers ROME (rolling) and Rock (stable) editions with KDE Plasma.

calculate.name: Calculate Linux
calculate.description: A Gentoo-based distribution pre-configured for desktop, server, and enterprise use. Provides binary packages so you don't need to compile from source like vanilla Gentoo.

arcolinux.name: ArcoLinux
arcolinux.description: An educational Arch-based project with three tiers: ArcoLinux (full), ArcoLinuxD (minimal), and ArcoLinuxB (build your own). Extensive video tutorials for learning Arch.
pros: Three tiers from easy to advanced
Great stepping stone to pure Arch

trisquel.name: Trisquel
trisquel.description: An FSF-endorsed fully free distribution based on Ubuntu LTS. Ships only libre software — no proprietary firmware, drivers, or codecs. For free software purists.

guix.name: GNU Guix System
guix.description: An advanced distribution from the GNU Project using the Guix package manager (like Nix but using Guile Scheme). Fully reproducible, transactional, and 100% free software.
pros: Guile Scheme config (more readable than Nix)
cons: Hardware support limited by libre policy

vanillaos.name: Vanilla OS
vanillaos.description: An immutable Ubuntu-based distro using the Vib image builder and ABRoot for atomic transactions. Apx package manager can install from any distro's repos via containers.
pros: Apx can install packages from any distro

nitrux.name: Nitrux
nitrux.description: A Debian-based immutable distribution featuring the NX Desktop (customized KDE Plasma) and MauiKit applications. Beautiful defaults with a focus on AppImages and Flatpak.
cons: Learning curve for NX Desktop specifics
